w-it-022.title: Panini (Italian Sandwich)

instructions.1: For the biga, sprinkle the yeast over the water in a large bowl large enough to fit all of the ingredients, and let sit 5 to 10 minutes.
instructions.2: Add the flours, and stir to combine. (The dough may seem stiff, but will soften up as it sits.)
instructions.3: Cover the biga tightly with plastic wrap, and let it sit for 6 hours at room temperature.
instructions.4: Stir the biga, and refrigerate it until the next day, or at least 12 hours.
instructions.5: For the buns, combine the flour, salt, and yeast in a large bowl.
instructions.6: Add the water and biga, and stir until the dough is mixed. (It will be quite wet, and rough in texture.)
instructions.7: Turn the dough out onto a floured counter or breadboard, and using as little flour as possible, knead for 5 minutes, or until the dough is smooth. (Don't worry that your dough still seems very loose and moist, as it will firm up as it rises.)
instructions.8: Place the dough into a large bowl three times the size of the dough that has been lightly oiled first.
instructions.9: Cover tightly with plastic wrap, and let sit in a warm spot for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, or until the dough has doubled, punching down and turning the dough every 30 minutes or so.
instructions.10: If using baking sheets, sprinkle them lightly with cornmeal.
instructions.11: Divide the dough into balls about 3 inches in diameter.
instructions.12: Work with your hands until they are evenly shaped.
instructions.13: Lightly roll in extra flour and place on your prepared baking sheet or bread peel.
instructions.14: Lightly press each ball with the heel of your hand to create a disc shape.
instructions.16: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
instructions.17: Fill a shallow casserole dish with water and place in the oven 10 minutes before you place the buns into the oven.
instructions.18: After 45 minutes, place the baking sheets into the hot oven, or move the buns with the peel onto the hot baking stone.
instructions.19: Bake for about 20 minutes, rotating the buns once during this time, or until the dough is a light golden brown all over.
instructions.20: Remove and let cool on a wire rack.

w-it-022.culturalNotes: Panini is a type of small Italian bread, commonly used for making sandwiches.
